Q: emacs/elisp: What is the hash (pound, number sign, octothorpe) symbol used for? A:

There is a difference if you want to pass a closure around:

(setq lexical-binding t)

(defun foo () (message "outer"))
(let ((x 5))
  (cl-flet ((foo () (message "inner: %d" (+ x x))))
    (setq y 'foo)
    (setq z #'foo)))
(funcall y)
(funcall z)

Outputs

outer
inner: 10

Though I think that's only because the cl-flet macro has special handling for #' aka (function ...). When you macroexpand it you get:

(let*
    ((--cl-foo--
      (cl-function
       (lambda nil
         (message "inner: %d"
                  (+ x x))))))
  (progn
    (message "%S" #''foo)
    (setq y 'foo)
    (setq z --cl-foo--)))

Q: WTF Flask dynamically built forms. How to deal with name attribute A:

Use FieldList with FormField to bundle value and metadata

The issue is that you are trying to bake metadata (unique_info_x) into the input's name attribute, which breaks how WTForms maps incoming data to form objects.

Instead of manipulating names, the "WTForms way" is to use a FormField inside your FieldList. This allows you to group the integer input and the unique identifier together.

1. Define a Sub-Form

Create a small form class to represent one "slot". Use a HiddenField to store your unique suffix.

from flask_wtf import FlaskForm
from wtforms import FieldList, IntegerField, HiddenField, FormField
from wtforms.validators import NumberRange

class SlotEntryForm(FlaskForm):
    # This stores your unique_info_x
    unique_info = HiddenField()
    # This is your numeric input
    value = IntegerField('Value', validators=[NumberRange(message='Insert numbers')])

    # Disable CSRF for sub-forms to avoid token redundancy
    class Meta:
        csrf = False

class SlotInputForm(FlaskForm):
    slots = FieldList(FormField(SlotEntryForm))

2. Handle the Route

Now, when you iterate over form.slots, each entry is an object containing both the value and the metadata.

@app.route('/', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def mainpage():
    form = SlotInputForm()

    if form.validate_on_submit():
        for entry in form.slots:
            # Access them cleanly as data attributes
            suffix = entry.unique_info.data
            val = entry.value.data
            print(f"Suffix: {suffix}, Value: {val}")
        
        return "Success!"

    return render_template('index.html', form=form)

Headline: Use FieldList with FormField to bundle value and metadata

Python

@app.route('/', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def mainpage():

        for entry in form.slots:
            # Access them cleanly as data attributes

3. Updated Template (Jinja2)

WTForms will automatically generate names like slots-0-unique_info and slots-0-value. You don't need to manually construct them in Javascript.

<form method="POST">
    {{ form.hidden_tag() }}
    <ul id="slots">
        {% for entry in form.slots %}
            <li>
                {{ entry.unique_info() }}  {# Hidden ID #}
                {{ entry.value() }}        {# Integer Input #}
            </li>
        {% endfor %}
    </ul>
    <input type="submit" value="Submit">
</form>

Why this is better:

  • Validation: form.validate() now automatically checks all numeric inputs in the list.

  • No String Splitting: You no longer need to "splice" the name string to find the ID.

  • Hidden Metadata: Using a HiddenField is the standard way to pass technical IDs back and forth without showing them to the user as labels.

Q: Python web scraping tool works on simple sites but fails on sites with anti-bot protections A:

Some problems can be resolved using Selenium to control real web browser (Chrome/Firefox) because it has all needed headers, and it can run JavaScript.

But sometimes web pages can even detect that you use Selenium and uses Captcha, etc. There are methods which try to hide this - e.g. undetected-chromedriver

For rate limiting you may have to run code with longer (random) delays - it has to behave more like real human.
